title: Meet a P&G Innovator Advancing the Science of Everyday Care
summary: P&G innovator Mark Sivik applies chemistry, materials science and consumer understanding to create breakthroughs across Fabric & Home Care.
body_markdown:
Through the partnership, Sivik and his research partners studied how detergent and stain-removal products performed aboard the ISS. Testing showed that the detergent maintained its consistency and that Tide To-Go Wipes and Tide To-Go Pens effectively removed stains including sriracha, coffee, olive oil and punch. Sivik also worked with NASA researchers at its 3D-printed Mars habitat in Houston, Texas, to explore and refine cleaning solutions for deep-space missions.


Sivik’s passion for innovation began when he was a teenager. After discovering an aptitude for math and chemistry, he set out to use those skills to benefit society, a purpose that continues to shape his work today. His approach starts with consumer needs and a willingness to pursue unconventional solutions. “Perseverance and challenging oneself to step out of the norm can bring many new opportunities that drive consumer delight through new technologies and processes,” he says.


Sivik emphasizes the importance of working across functions and with external partners to advance discoveries. “By removing constraints and enrolling others and sharing accountability, even some of the hardest projects that require breakthrough can be achieved,” he says.


For Sivik, innovation extends beyond his career; it is also a way of life. Through hobbies such as sports, photography, and cooking, he continues to experiment, across many touch points strengthening the curiosity and creativity he brings to his work.


From everyday cleaning challenges to his past work addressing the demands of deep-space missions, Sivik demonstrates how curiosity, collaboration and science can unlock innovations that improve life now and in the future.
